newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian miners killed in mine flood.
newsitem.headline: Australian miners killed in mine flood.

text.p: Four Australian coal miners were killed on Thursday when the tunnel they were working in flooded, police said.

The accident at the Gretley colliery in the Hunter Valley north of Sydney occured at about 5.30 a.m. (1830 GMT) when the miners broke through into old works which caused flooding, a police spokesman told Reuters.
Four other miners, working some 120 metres (558 feet) underground, were hit by the flood waters but survived. No names have been released.
It is unclear how many miners were working underground at the time of the accident or whether there were other casualties.

The mine in the Hunter Valley, Australia's second largest coal district, is owned by Oakbridge Ltd. Oakbridge is 42-percent owned by the U.S. Cyprus-Amax mining group, the second largest coal producer in the United States, which has been expanding its coal operations in Australia.
